lines.text: This is Math Explorer, a Star Learner game that makes math visible. Every number is a set of blocks you can count, and every answer is spoken out loud.

Operation tiles sit across the bottom: addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division. Story games stack on the right: chickens and eggs, two trains, and the coin counter. The menu tile holds every tutorial, and the help tile is always there if you need a reminder.

Every operation has a block tutorial. She counts red blocks, watches four slide away for take-away, sees three groups of four become twelve, and shares nine blocks into three buckets. The blocks do the teaching.

The games are little movies she can play. Hens lay eggs into hatch beds, then she packs the cartons. Two trains race, and she answers how far ahead the fast one gets. Pennies, nickels, and dimes make the amount.

Practice mode asks fresh questions forever. She can tap the blocks to count them, then choose from three big answers. A wrong answer is never just wrong. The blocks slowly count themselves out, so she sees exactly why.
Math Explorer. Numbers she can see, touch, and count. Ready to play on the Star Learner console.
